chart.1.5:
1.5-year-old (yearling)
- Neck and neck-shoulder junction: Thin neck; a distinct line of separation between the neck and shoulders and little muscle definition (NDA 2012). Lower edge of the neck joins the body high up on the chest (NDA cards). Will not develop the swollen neck and muscular characteristics of older bucks (MSU P2206). No neck swelling (MDWFP). Thin necks (TPWD 2004).
- Chest/brisket depth: Chest, stomach, and neck are not fully developed (NDA 2012; NDA cards).
- Waist vs chest depth: Thin waist (NDA 2012). Body appears sleek, with no muscle definition (NDA cards).
- Belly line: Torso (stomach, chest, and neck) not fully developed (NDA 2012; NDA cards). The fetched 1.5 sections do not describe a sagging belly.
- Back/topline: The fetched 1.5 sections in NDA 2012, MSU P2206, MDWFP, and TPWD 2004 do not give a separate yearling back-line. NDA cards describe "Back and belly are flat or level, waistline is tight" as a 2.5 cue, not a 1.5 cue.
- Legs relative to body depth: Legs appear too long for their bodies because their torsos (stomach, chest, and neck) are not fully developed (NDA 2012). Legs appear too long in proportion because chest, stomach, and hindquarters are not fully developed (NDA cards). Long, thin legs (MSU P2206; MDWFP). Legs appear long and slender, and their torso is slim like a doe's (TPWD 2004).
- Hindquarters vs chest: Thin hindquarters (MSU P2206). CONFLICT on the comparison: NDA cards say hindquarters appear larger and higher than chest/shoulders. These two are not the same comparison; both are given.
- Overall shape: Looks like a doe with antlers (NDA 2012; NDA cards; MSU P2206; MDWFP). Appear dainty, with baby faces and thin necks; if the antlers are covered in a photo, the body resembles a doe (TPWD 2004).
chart.2.5:
2.5-year-old
- Neck and neck-shoulder junction: Slight swelling in their neck during the rut (NDA 2012). Minimal neck swelling during the rut; neck still joins the chest high on the shoulders at a distinct junction (NDA cards). A limited amount of neck swelling due to muscle development (MSU P2206; MDWFP). Necks appear stretched in proportion (TPWD 2004).
- Chest/brisket depth: Relatively thin waist and shoulders (NDA cards). Slim shoulders (MDWFP). Relatively thin neck, chest, and waist (MSU P2206 photo caption).
- Waist vs chest depth: Their waist is still thin (NDA 2012). Relatively thin waist and shoulders (NDA cards). The waist, or area just in front of the back legs, is relatively thin (MSU P2206). Relative thin long waist with a thicker hindquarter (MDWFP).
- Belly line: Back and belly are flat or level, waistline is tight (NDA cards). The fetched 2.5 sections do not describe a sagging belly.
- Back/topline: Back and belly are flat or level (NDA cards).
- Legs relative to body depth: Legs still appear too long for their bodies; overall sleek appearance (NDA 2012). Legs still appear slightly long for body (NDA cards). Gangly and awkward; legs appear to be growing too fast for their body; legs and necks appear stretched in proportion (TPWD 2004). Legs appear long and lanky (MSU P2206; MDWFP).
- Hindquarters vs chest: Hindquarters proportional to chest/shoulder area (NDA cards). Hindquarters are much more filled in than the yearling's (MSU P2206). Thicker hindquarter with slim shoulders (MDWFP).
- Overall shape: Overall sleek appearance (NDA 2012; NDA cards). Gangly and awkward (TPWD 2004).
chart.3.5:
3.5-year-old
- Neck and neck-shoulder junction: Muscled shoulders and a highly swelled neck during the rut (NDA 2012). Thickly muscled neck during the rut, but still a slight separation between neck and shoulders (NDA cards). During the rut, the buck's neck is thickly muscled, yet there is still a distinct junction between the neck and shoulders (MSU P2206; Outdoor Alabama). Neck is thick and muscled during the rut but still a distinction between the neck and shoulders (MDWFP). Neck muscles are expanding from increased hormones and use during the rut but are still not as large or thick as a fully mature buck; the neck is still distinct by four or five inches from their brisket (TPWD 2004).
- Chest/brisket depth: A deep chest and lean waist (NDA 2012). Chest/shoulder area begins to look heavier than hindquarters (NDA cards). The chest region may begin to appear deeper than the hindquarter area (MSU P2206). Chest region will be deeper than the hindquarters and waist (MDWFP). Their chest is beginning to appear larger than their rump (TPWD 2004). Chest appears deeper than the hindquarters, giving the appearance of a well-conditioned racehorse (Outdoor Alabama).
- Waist vs chest depth: Their waist is still lean (NDA 2012). Waistline still tight (NDA cards). Chest deeper than the hindquarters and waist (MDWFP).
- Belly line: Taut back and stomach (MDWFP). Their back and stomach are still straight and taut (TPWD 2004). Not described as sagging at this age in NDA 2012, MSU P2206, MDWFP, or TPWD 2004.
- Back/topline: Taut back and stomach (MDWFP). Back and stomach are still straight and taut (TPWD 2004).
- Legs relative to body depth: Legs appear to be the right length for their bodies because their torsos are now more fully developed (NDA 2012; NDA cards). TPWD 2004 does not yet call 3.5 legs short; it saves "This is the first time their legs do not appear longer than they should" for 4.5.
- Hindquarters vs chest: Chest beginning to look heavier or deeper than the hindquarters or rump (NDA cards; MSU P2206; MDWFP; TPWD 2004; Outdoor Alabama).
- Overall shape: Three-year-olds are likened to middle linebackers: big and strong but also lean and fast. A deep chest and lean waist give them a "racehorse" appearance (NDA 2012). Prime-condition, athletic appearance, good muscle tone but still lanky and lean (NDA cards). Some biologists compare its look to that of a well-conditioned racehorse (MSU P2206).
chart.4.5:
4.5-year-old
- Neck and neck-shoulder junction: CONFLICT on whether the neck blends at 4.5. MSU P2206: the neck region is fully muscled, giving the appearance of blending into the shoulders. MDWFP: fully muscled neck that blends into the shoulders. Outdoor Alabama: fully muscled neck blends into the shoulders, and waist is deep as chest. NDA 2012: fully-muscled shoulders and heavy swelling in their neck during the rut, without the word "blends." TPWD 2004's 4.5 paragraph does not say the neck blends into the shoulders or brisket; that "one continuous muscle" line is in its 5.5 section.
- Chest/brisket depth: Stomachs, chests, and necks are now fully developed (NDA 2012). MSU P2206 photo caption: showing the blending of neck, chest, and waist areas.
- Waist vs chest depth: Their waist has dropped down to become even with their chest (NDA 2012). The waistline is as deep as the chest (MSU P2206; MDWFP; Outdoor Alabama). CONFLICT / gap: TPWD 2004's 4.5 paragraph does not state that the waist is even with the chest.
- Belly line: Not described as sagging at 4.5 in NDA 2012, MSU P2206, MDWFP, or TPWD 2004. TPWD calls the 4.5 body muscular and lean. Sag, pot belly, or a dropped belly is reserved for older classes in those guides.
- Back/topline: Not described as sagging or swayed at 4.5 in NDA 2012, MSU P2206, MDWFP, or TPWD 2004.
- Legs relative to body depth: CONFLICT. NDA 2012: most four-year-olds have legs that appear too short for their body. TPWD 2004: this is the first time their legs do not appear longer than they should for their body; their legs may even appear slightly short for the thickened body. MDWFP: legs will look proportionate to the body. MSU P2206 does not give a separate 4.5 leg-length line; it saves "His legs appear shorter than legs of younger deer, but this is an optical illusion because his chest is taking up more of the viewing area" for 5.5- to 6.5-year-olds.
- Hindquarters vs chest: Implied by the lost racehorse look and by a waist now as deep as the chest (MSU P2206; NDA 2012). The fetched 4.5 sections do not give a separate hindquarter-versus-chest comparison beyond that.
- Overall shape: Four-year-olds have an entirely different appearance than one- to three-year-old bucks. Because their stomachs, chests, and necks are now fully developed, most four-year-olds have legs that appear too short for their body (NDA 2012). White-tailed bucks physiologically mature by 4.5 years of age; they have almost all of the adult body mass and have lost the racehorse look (MSU P2206). When bucks reach 4 1/2, they attain skeletal maturity and begin exhibiting many characteristics of full maturity. Their bodies have reached full size but are muscular and lean (TPWD 2004).
chart.5.5:
5.5-year-old and older (prime). NDA 2012 groups 5.5 to 7.5 years. MSU P2206 groups 5.5- to 6.5-year-olds as mature or prime and treats 7.5 and older separately. MDWFP has a 5.5+ fully mature line and a separate overmature line. TPWD 2004 gives separate 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, and post-maturity paragraphs. Overmature signs are listed at the end so they are not required to match this 5.5+ class.
- Neck and neck-shoulder junction: Heavy swelling in their neck during the rut (NDA 2012, same words as at 4.5). During the rut, the buck's neck blends completely into his shoulders (MSU P2206). Neck completely blends into the shoulders, and the neck and brisket will appear to be one (MDWFP). TPWD 2004 at 5.5: their neck will swell considerably during the rut, making the neck and brisket appear to be one continuous muscle; their neck, while being very big, will appear muscular and firm and not flabby.
- Chest/brisket depth: The neck and brisket will appear to be one (MDWFP). Neck and brisket appear to be one continuous muscle (TPWD 2004, 5.5). Front half appears to be one large mass (MSU P2206; Outdoor Alabama). Shoulders will look bigger than the rump area (MDWFP).
- Waist vs chest depth: NDA 2012 says 5.5 to 7.5 still have a waist that's even with their chest, plus the pot belly / sagging back that 4.5 may not have. MSU P2206 and MDWFP do not restate the waist-even line at 5.5; they add sagging belly (and, for MDWFP, short legs and neck-and-brisket as one).
- Belly line: Agreement that sag or a pot belly belongs here or later, not at 4.5; wording differs by source. NDA 2012 (5.5-7.5): they also may have a pot belly and a sagging back. MSU P2206 (5.5-6.5): most mature bucks exhibit a sagging belly. MDWFP (5.5+): sagging belly and battle scars are usually evident. Outdoor Alabama (5.5-6.5): most exhibit prominent potbelly. TPWD 2004 (5.5): typically their stomach and back have a noticeable sag. TPWD 2004 (6.5): throughout most of the year they will have a sagging stomach, except during the post-rut due to weight loss.
- Back/topline: CONFLICT on whether the back already sags at 5.5. NDA 2012 (5.5-7.5) may have a pot belly and a sagging back. TPWD 2004 (5.5): stomach and back have a noticeable sag; (6.5): their back will also sag, making their front shoulders appear taller. MSU P2206 places "a swayed back and a prominent potbelly" under 7.5-year-old and older, not under 5.5-6.5. MDWFP places "swayed back and a potbelly" under overmature.
- Legs relative to body depth: NDA 2012: bucks in this category have legs that appear too short for their body. MSU P2206: his legs appear shorter than legs of younger deer, but this is an optical illusion because his chest is taking up more of the viewing area. MDWFP: legs will appear short for the body. TPWD 2004 at 5.5: legs will appear short almost to an exaggerated extent, due to the fuller and fatter bodies.
- Hindquarters vs chest: Shoulders will look bigger than the rump area (MDWFP). Front half appears to be one large mass (MSU P2206).
- Overall shape: Their increased body mass gives them a more rounded appearance, and they may look like a small cow (NDA 2012). During the rut, the buck's neck blends completely into his shoulders, and his front half appears to be one large mass (MSU P2206; Outdoor Alabama). The neck and brisket will appear to be one; shoulders will look bigger than the rump area (MDWFP).
- Overmature (later than this 5.5+ prime class, only where a source splits it): loose skin on the face, neck, and shoulders, usually visible as a chin flap, and pointed shoulder and hip bones (NDA 2012, 8.5 and older). Muscularity is lost in the neck area; a swayed back and a prominent potbelly; loose skin on the neck and head areas (MSU P2206, 7.5 and older). Swayed back and a potbelly are common along with loose skin due to lack of muscle (MDWFP, overmature). TPWD 2004, post-maturity: knocked knees, noticeably sagging stomachs, and swayed backs with a hump above the shoulders.
